prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: Earth-observation land/coastal/cryosphere products; predictable latency/documented quality. Ground excludes spacecraft/launch/external processing except interfaces. Elements: Mission Control Center (Bluebell, local voice only): operations/pass supervision/anomalies/human-authorized validated-command release/contact schedule. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral, legacy logs): orbit/maneuver analysis; access/navigation/visibility/antenna-pointing products→planning before execution release. Mission Planning System: approved demand/constraints→routine plans; receives Contact booking requests specifying service/antenna preference/minimum elevation/volume/priority. Command Validation Gateway: mandatory plan-to-uplink rule barrier. Network Control System: connectivity/routing; distributes station allocations, confirms readiness, records actual contact start/end. Ground Network Manager (Juniper, rosters): availability/compatibility; arbitrates conflicts, verifies maintenance/staffing commitments; issues Antenna Deicing Notice for threatening icing. Telemetry Ingest Service: scheduled spacecraft telemetry→operations/engineering/processing; receives contact-status/data-flow indicators distinguishing planned gaps/station interruptions. Orbit Determination Engine: tracking→controlled orbit knowledge; qualified tracking pass→Doppler Residual Report for navigation trends. Payload Processing Facility: processing/calibration/assessment/distribution; coordinates allocation-driven load/delivery changes with Primary Processing Cluster (nominal) and Backup Processing Cluster (controlled failover). Product Quality Service: automated/analyst pre-dissemination checks. Long Term Archive: authoritative data/products/records/traceability. User Services Portal: controlled search/order/status/support. Antennas: North S-Band Antenna—early-pass uplink/low-rate telemetry/conservative margins; South S-Band Antenna—procedure-compatible short-notice alternate; Kiruna X-Band Antenna—European high-rate downlink/contact margins; Svalbard X-Band Antenna—northern/longer visibility/lower elevation loss. Actors: Spacecraft Operations Team—safety/authorization/contact/contingencies; Flight Dynamics Team—navigation/orbit maintenance; Payload Calibration Team—calibration/performance/quality; Cybersecurity Desk—continuous security/escalation; Local station teams—configuration/frequency/time/interlocks/anomaly logs; Station operators—constraint notifications→Mission Control Center. Rules: daily-cutoff routine freeze; later contingencies require recorded justification. Conflict precedence: safety>timeliness>resource efficiency. Forecast/measured wind/precipitation/temperature/lightning/attenuation govern weather decisions; X-band

New part:
S051: Performance trends for each antenna are reviewed at regular operations meetings so that recurring acquisition delays, pointing errors, or link-margin shortfalls are converted into corrective actions.
S052: The wide area connectivity design extends the ground network management practices from the scheduling domain into continuous transport control across all operational sites.
S053: The physical topology uses redundant terrestrial circuits between the Mission Control Center, the Flight Dynamics Facility, the Payload Processing Facility, and the Long Term Archive, with diverse carrier entrances where local infrastructure permits.
S054: The North S-Band Antenna and the South S-Band Antenna connect to the Mission Control Center through protected access routers that keep command and telemetry traffic separate from site administration traffic.
S055: The Kiruna X-Band Antenna and the Svalbard X-Band Antenna use dual wide area paths toward the Payload Processing Facility so that payload downlink traffic can continue during a single carrier outage.
S056: The Mission Control Center hosts the primary routing policy point, while the Network Control System maintains operational visibility of circuit state, path selection, and active maintenance windows.
S057: The Network Control System is known operationally as Lantern and is treated as the authoritative view of wide area circuit status.
S058: Routing policy is based on approved prefixes, authenticated neighbor relationships, and deterministic preference values rather than ad hoc route changes during contacts.
S059: Dynamic routing is permitted only on controlled adjacencies, and static backup routes are preconfigured for antenna sites where local carrier behavior is not sufficiently predictable.
S060: Critical contact paths are pinned before acquisition of signal when the Ground Network Manager determines that a maintenance condition could cause route oscillation.
S061: Management access to routers, firewalls, time servers, and monitoring probes is restricted to dedicated administration networks that are not advertised to mission data enclaves.
S062: Latency budgets are assigned by service class so that command validation, real-time telemetry display, orbit determination support, processing transfers, and archive replication can be measured against different expectations.
S063: The budget for real-time command and telemetry traffic between the Mission Control Center, the Command Validation Gateway, and the Telemetry Ingest Service is managed as an end-to-end figure that includes encryption overhead and firewall inspection time.
S064: Traffic supporting the Orbit Determination Engine is given a tighter jitter objective than routine file movement because late or uneven delivery can reduce the usefulness of contact assessment products.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
